top_categories.workout_context: Road-specific control matters at GFNY Walnut Creek. Practice on technical rolling roads into a major summit finish: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 64 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic GFNY Walnut Creek's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before April.
At GFNY Walnut Creek, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
107ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
6,909ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
6,909ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at GFNY Walnut Creek. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of GFNY Walnut Creek. Train it until it feels boring.

Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on technical rolling roads into a major summit finish can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
64 miles on technical rolling roads into a major summit finish burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
Low-cadence force work supports 6,909ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.
Smooth pedaling at 64 miles saves muscle. Bad technique at mile 10 is invisible. At mile 80 it's a cramp.

race_overlay.nutrition: Use training to rehearse an eating and drinking plan for GFNY Walnut Creek's 64 miles. Start early and use products you tolerate. Use the organizer's current resupply plan for final carry decisions.
race_overlay.altitude: Altitude may change sustainable power and recovery at GFNY Walnut Creek. Use conservative pacing and test any travel strategy before the event.
race_overlay.terrain: The technical descents at GFNY Walnut Creek demand practice on similar paved roads. Ride technical rolling roads into a major summit finish at race-day cadence weekly. Practice braking points, corner entry, line choice, and accelerating smoothly out of turns. Confirm tire pressure and equipment before race week.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Road Specific, Race Simulation, and Over Under to prepare you for 64 miles of technical rolling roads into a major summit finish in Walnut Creek, California, USA.
